WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
This package comes with two bags of pens. There are two of each color in each bag for a total of 4 each color:
Black
Red
Neon Green
Yellow
Purple
Royal Blue
Neon Pink

HOW ARE THESE MADE?
The caps each have a light in them with a paper tab to remove when it is time to use one. The top has a little light in it that if you press a button on the side, the light goes on. The pen itself is white like a marker type.

HOW DO THESE WORK?
The pens write clear- almost a tiny tinge of green like glow in the dark paint tends to be. It allows you to see a little of what you are writing. When you turn the cap on- the writing lights up and it is very easy to read.

DO THESE WORK UNDER BLACKLIGHT?
Yes, if you were to decorate something that you plan to have in a blacklight room (halloween, lessons, parties, etc), the writing will show up when the blacklights come on. It would be great for a mystery theater too.

HOW POPULAR WERE THESE?
The kids LOVE these. It keeps them busy for a little while anyway. They also made a nice prize for games.

THE BOTTOM LINE
A great item to have on hand for a variety of reasons- from kids and parties, to mystery theaters, these markers are delightful. I love the colors they come in too- the writing is all the same, just the outside is different.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS! I personally love to play with these as much as all of the kids do!

Hot Wheels T-Rex Rampage Track Set, Works City Sets, Toys for Boys Ages 5 to 10 My son has several sets of Hot Wheels toys. Hot Wheels is often hit or miss. They sometimes have a great idea and an awesomely executed toy. Sometimes the toys create nothing but frustration. However, with this playset my really had nothing but fear. Therefore, the Mattel Hot Wheels City T-Rex Rampage has done it's job. It strikes fear in all those who come upon it. My 7 year old is afraid of this toy. He was ok with it until he found out that the T-Rex moved, and it's no dice. He doesn't even want it just sitting in his room.

After you figure out how to put it together. The T-Rex part was tricky, but don't worry the part can come apart so if you mess up the alignment, you're ok. You get 1 angry T-Rex who needs a snack and a nap, 2 buildings, a launchpad, and a piece of track and a car. I'm not sure what the name of the game is. I am not entirely sure what you are supposed to do. My son comes up with different ideas every 5 minutes. However, the scary part comes in when you turn it on. The toy comes with batteries and when you turn it on and push the blue button on the circle track, the T-Rex will start to thrash around and knock over buildings etc. He roars and all of this action is what scares my son. The launcher is of course his favorite part. If you launch the car just right, the car will hit a button to "defeat" the dinosaur.

The ultimate issue with Hot Wheels is that except for the cars themselves, most sets get broken fairly quickly. I cannot say the same for this because it's not getting much play. As with all Hot Wheel sets you can connect them to each other if you have enough track to do so. So, that is the best part about Hot Wheels. However, tracks are hard to come by and they are usually long and flimsy. So, you can't really link up the sets and the tracks get all bent out of shape. So, this will connect to the other sets we have. However, that is only great thing about it. I don't really get the whole dinosaurs or mutant alligators are taking over the city. Neither does my son. I'm all for imagination, but this whole concept seems to have been created in a vacuum. There is no background story, nothing. My son asked why is the T-Rex in the city. I had nothing.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels T-Rex Rampage Track Set, Works City Sets, Toys for Boys Ages 5 to 10

Forbidden Island – The Cooperative Strategy Survival Island Board Game,2-4 players My wife and I bought this as we are getting more into tabletop gaming (thanks Wil and Felicia!) and I wanted something adventurous and less involved than a city- farm- building simulation game.
This is fairly fun, but the main reason I am writing a review is to specify why I didn't give it four stars and who should get the most enjoyment out of it.
To start out, you choose (randomly for a bit of extra challenge) a character class. These are more realistic classes such as a SCUBA diver, rather than a mage or warrior. Each class has a different special ability, for example the diver can traverse water tiles more easily than other classes. Then you randomly generate the playing field by placing the heavier island cards in a specific formation. Combining the random character roles and the random board is a clever way to make every game different and make sure the players have to think critically rather than relying too much on rote strategies.
Your goal is to traverse the board to collect treasures, cooperating with your fellow players by using each person's ability and the convenience of their position on the board. You may even bail each other out of dire situations by airlifting them to safety or using your special ability, because while you are trying to reach the treasures the island is constantly flooding.
If you ever wanted to play Indiana Jones this is a pretty good start. But for my wife and I to keep it interesting, we have to play on the hardest difficulty level (starting out with more of the island in a flooded state) and even still we have succeeded at our task 100% of the time. Because of this, the game gets old too quickly, which is a shame since the premise is fun, the concept is exciting, the gameplay is perfectly tight, and the artwork is gorgeous.
I do think there is a more appropriate audience for this, which is kids of perhaps 9 years to 13 years playing with other kids or in a mixed group with adults. I think the game will be more challenging for kids and I think playing with kids will make it more fun for the parents/cousins/uncles and aunts etc.
For two adults who are strategy-oriented people, there are more complicated games that are perhaps less beautiful and tightly designed but nonetheless more consistently engaging.
text_fidelity_b: Forbidden Island – The Cooperative Strategy Survival Island Board Game,2-4 players

After about 5 minutes of getting used to this tiny drone it hit the wall (4 feet up in the air) and slid down to the floor. I turned it off and redid the start up procedure to get more practice controlling the drone. OH NO!!! all it does now is goes side ways and immediately lunges towards the floor. I can not believe how simple it is to destroy this plastic drone. I am a very cautious adult, thus buying this HS340 so that I would have experience under my belt before using a $150 dollar HS175D ( much better than the HS175) drone. I wanted to buy my HD175D from amazon but the D version was on e-xxx  dot com website for less money (after making an offer) and better camera plus better bearings. Now I see that the return window is closed so I will simply throw this $35 (sale price) dollar paper weight in the trash. I guess I can not in good conscience recommend this drone unless you are prepared to use it only in a space that can not hit a wall at 4 foot height. So not very likely. I am quite disappointed with Holy Stone products overall.

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show is a fun way for your little fashion diva to spend some free time. All you do is download the application on your smartphone, tablet, or iPod touch, draw some fashion designs, and then scan them. Your fashion will then show up on an actual fashion model, in 3D, to your child’s delight.

My girls are fashion designers in the making so I knew they would love playing with the Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show. It takes little effort to get going. You just add the application to your smartphone or tablet, and then have your child start drawing. Once scanned through the application, kids will be able to see their own fashion design on an actual model. This caused squeals of satisfaction from my girls who loved seeing their fashion on screen.

From my children’s perspectives, there is little that isn’t perfect with a toy like this, but as an adult, I can see a few issues. One has already been stated by others who have used the device, but bears repeating: The phone or tablet you use will make a difference. Not all smartphones or tablets are created equally and the colors may look a little off. If you have more than one device and it doesn’t look good on one, then you might want to consider downloading the application to another device. It could make a difference and it’s simple enough to do.

The included accessories with the Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show are a little limited. The small colored pencils are also somewhat of an obstacle, as they are not good for larger hands. But overall, this is a fun fashion design kit and I cannot imagine a fashion- loving child who wouldn’t fall in love with it.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show

text_fidelity_a:
SKLZ Pro Mini Basketball Hoop A simple way to amuse and practice your shot, the SKLZ Pro Mini Basketball Hoop offers glow in the dark appeal, easy assembly, and hours of fun. It hooks on the top of most doors so you can lie in bed and practice shooting or attach it to your office door at work for some quick stress relief.

Out of the box, this basketball hoop requires some assembly, but it shouldn’t take long to attach the parts and prep it for use. The hooks that attach it to a door are not adjustable, but they are designed to fit a wide range of door thicknesses. After attaching, you may notice that it lacks stability. I noticed it, too, but I also found that it didn’t matter. It doesn’t need to be completely stable because the weight of the included basketball is so light. Throw after throw results in no bouncing or other movement for me, so don’t worry if the hoop seems less secure than you would prefer. Unless your door is very thin, it should be fine.

Once you have the ball inflated, the toy is ready for use. You may want to set everything in direct light for a few hours at first, to help with the glowing. If you don’t, then the glow will be very faint. Still, it should be enough to make it visible in the dark so that, if you use this at home, you or your kids can see it in the dark and play before you fall asleep. One thing that new buyers need to realize is that, due to the thickness of the hooks, it may not be possible to close the door to which this is attached. My door won’t close, but I attached it to a door that normally stays open all of the time anyway. If your door won’t close with this attached, then you will have no choice but to go back and forth, taking it down and putting it back up.

Overall, this seems like a good toy and it should be fun for the basketball enthusiast in your home. There is no glass and the construction is made to last. The glow in the dark feature could be better, but other than that, it seems like an entertaining way to pass the time.
text_fidelity_b: SKLZ Pro Mini Basketball Hoop

If your child loves Fortnite characters and likes action, then he/she will love the Fortnite Baller Vehicle.

When I first saw this toy, I thought the clear globe inside the box was just for show but it is actually part of the vehicle. Contained inside is one Fortnite figure and the base that the figure and globe rest on is the actual vehicle itself. It comes with a remote control and you have to load batteries into both the vehicle and the remote control before you can use it.

With the remote control in hand, the Fortnite Baller Vehicle is ready for action. The remote has two knobs on it, similar to the controller for home video games. Kids can move each knob and control the movement of the vehicle. I discovered, too, that there is an adjustment level underneath that you can use if the vehicle isn’t moving the way you want it to. And since the inside accommodates Fortnite figures, kids can feel free to swap out the one that comes with this toy with another one from the set.

Fortnite fans have any number of toys they can buy that feature their favorite Fortnite characters, but the Fortnite Baller Vehicle is one of the cooler ones available. The remote-controlled movement sets this toy apart and it’s a great choice for fans of these action figures.

Disney Pixar Toy Story 4 Stunt Racer Duke Caboom Figure, 5.9 in, in Racing Outfit with Motorcycle and Launcher, Race Up to 15 ft and Perform Stunts, Gift for 3 Years and Older [[VIDEOID:3bd077e56d6c98a9858470ee43cf995]] This figure looks great, is very faithful to the movie & is very pose-able with 20 points of articulation. With the motorcycle it offers a lot of play-ability. The figure fits the bike very well & can be posed in many ways on the bike. There are several pegs on the bike that fit into holes in Duke's boots to make him at least look balanced. Duke's helmet doesn't come off.
The stunt cycle's performance is also faithful to the movie which is unfortunate. The launcher is more of a gimmick & isn't necessary to use the toy. All of the cycle's motivation comes from winding a spring inside the bike by rolling it backwards. It's actually hard to put the bike in the launcher after it is wound without releasing the stored energy.
The motorcycle isn't quite as detailed or faithful to the movie but it looks great & it can take a beating without breaking. The cycle also has an extendable stand & set of dolly wheels that allows it to emulate a wheel stand while either rolling or just posing.
I wasn't able to get this to any kids before the review but I think it will be fun as a standalone or addition to other Toy Story character dolls. I can't think of any other full size dolls from the franchise that come with a vehicle.

Melissa & Doug Wooden Stamp Set: Vehicles - 10 Stamps, 5 Colored Pencils, 2-Color Stamp Pad Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is a fun toy that encourages creativity and keeps kids occupied. This stamp kit comes complete with nine different stamps, a small ink pad with pink and purple ink, and five colored pencils for your child's creative enjoyment.

Melissa and Doug toys are known for education, creativity, and durability and most every product the company makes can be counted on to posses at least two of these qualities. The same is true with this toy. The Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set isn't big on educational quality, but it does encourage creativity and the set and storage container are made from wood, for better durability. The wooden container offers easy storage so that pieces do not get lost and the product's individual pieces are designed to last.

Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is simple yet fun and requires little supervision or explaining. My little princesses like this toy and still find it fun, but I have noticed that it lacks the staying power of some of their favorite toys. Unless I suggest it, they are not likely to use it. They do like it, but I think they have become a little bored with it. They prefer toys with movement and sound, and this offers neither.

This stamp set is certainly durable, but one thing that isn't made to last is the ink pad. I like that the Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set comes complete with its own ink and my girls strongly appreciate that the ink is colored purple and pink. However, don't expect the ink to last very long. The small blotches of ink will not offer many stamping adventures, so be prepared to purchase additional ink stamps within a few months.

Although not the perfect toy, the Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is nonetheless a good toy for little princesses everywhere. It has many positive qualities, encourages creativity, and is priced right. Like I said, it lacks staying power, but it has enough positive qualities to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Wooden Stamp Set: Vehicles - 10 Stamps, 5 Colored Pencils, 2-Color Stamp Pad

text_fidelity_a:
Money Savvy Pig - Pink Money Savvy Pig offers a fun and effective way to teach kids about money and its many important uses. Parents devote very little time to the concept of financial management, in spite of its critical nature, often because they are not sure how best to approach the subject. Money Savvy Pig makes it easy to introduce youngsters to these important concepts.

How does Money Savvy Pig work as an educational device? The answer is simple. By including four different chambers with different labels- one for spend, one for save, one for donate, and one for invest- kids gain a sense of financial management and money allocation. They learn that money has uses that go far beyond ordinary spending. Kids under the age of seven are not ready to learn the specifics of these different concepts, but early exposure is a good idea and the Money Savvy Bank Pig certainly succeeds in this respect.

The Money Savvy Bank is made from plastic and mine has held up fine thus far. Others have pointed out that this bank can break if dropped on a hard surface. Considering its lightweight design, it isn't difficult to imagine the bank breaking apart if mishandled, which is why parents need to exercise caution and make sure their kids handle the bank with extra care when moving from one place to the next.

I like that this bank separates money into four different sections and I like that it gets kids thinking about money and its uses. One limitation, however, is that this bank isn't very good for storing paper money. The reason is because the pieces of paper are difficult to remove. The openings on the bottom of the bank are small- too small to stick your hand inside the bank to remove paper. Place a folded dollar bill inside this bank and it will take some shaking and maneuvering to remove it from the bottom. Thus, this bank should be avoided for storing paper currency. It is intended for use with coins.

Financial literacy is important and kids need to learn about money at the youngest age possible. The Money Savvy Pig is a very good piggy bank for youngsters and its benefits go far beyond the encouragement of savings. It encourages kids to ask questions and think about money in different ways, making it a great choice for a child's early financial education.
text_fidelity_b: Money Savvy Pig - Pink

Rolife DIY Book Nook Kits Time Travel, 3D Wooden Puzzles Bookshelf Insert Decorative Bookend Model Kits with LED, DIY Crafts/Birthday Gifts/Home Decor for Girls&Boys Teens&Adults (Time Travel) I've seen these decorative bookends before, but they're rather pricey. So when I saw one that wasn't as expensive and looked like it would be a fun project, I decided to give it a try. I've always enjoyed crafts and a recent project was assembling and decorating an entire dollhouse.
That project, which took a couple of months, was nowhere near as frustrating as this, which took two days (when I'm determined, I'm determined).
Note that there's only ONE bookend in the kit. The first photo pictures two, but there's only one per kit. The kit comes with glue, a screwdriver, two lights, instructions, and everything you need except the batteries to power the lights. I would HIGHLY recommend that you provide a strong glue such as super glue or a really good wood glue for this project. You'll need it if my experience is anything to go by while building it.
I also recommend that you don't pop out the pieces beforehand, but do it while building (unless you are the type to label everything after you do that). There are a LOT of pieces to keep track of, and the labels aren't printed on them. Resist the temptation.
Now, for the kit itself. The instructions are NOT the best. There's 30+ pages, and very few words. It's basically illustrations and there were times when I feel steps were skipped. I had to figure out on my own which light when where (the shorter light for the door lamp, the longer one for the top light). Things like that. It was very frustrating.
Also, the kit is made out of a composite wood and has many, MANY tiny parts. Some parts that you have to push through tiny openings and through multiple openings. As careful as I was, these pieces broke. Hence the need for a really good, strong glue. The glue was also needed to keep pieces together. There were so many times that parts fell off when they shouldn't have, so gluing them together helped to move things along.
Oh, and I'd put pieces together only to have the instructions have pieces added later, and I'd be all 'why didn't they have me add this piece earlier'? Especially when you're pushing delicate pieces together.
If you've a miniature magnetic screwdriver, use it instead. The included screws are tiny and you're trying to get them in very small holes while screwing at awkward angles. Not having to worry about them falling will really help.
There was a lot of swearing involved with this project, I will not lie. I'm not sure this is a project for a kid, 14+ or older, unless they really like kit-building. Maybe if it was built out of better material. I debated what to rate it, but since it turned out looking good in the end (with the help of a lot of extra glue), I went with three stars. The finished product is lovely and the lights work, it was just very frustrating to get there.
text_fidelity_b: Rolife DIY Book Nook Kits Time Travel, 3D Wooden Puzzles Bookshelf Insert Decorative Bookend Model Kits with LED, DIY Crafts/Birthday Gifts/Home Decor for Girls&Boys Teens&Adults (Time Travel)

At first glance, the great hall looks impressive. But the plastic is the very cheap, brittle kind. The hall has a seam down the center so two sides can swing open and shut. The first time I set this up to look at it, the "doors" would not latch shut, and then once I did get them latched, the left side got stuck and did not want to open.There are lights that flash on and off for about 5 seconds when a button is pressed. The sorting hat is attached the the wall and you can place one of the four figures under it, but it doesn't do anything else as far as I know. There is a wand YOU CAN BUY SEPARATELY that works with this playset, but I don't know what the wand can do that you cannot do manually by pushing a button or sliding a figure along. The figures included look ok, and you get Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Professor Dumbledore. No bag guy figures are included, which I feel is a missed opportunity for more play scenarios. If they threw in a Voldemort or even Snape or Draco Malfoy, there would be an antagonist other than the snake who is stuck to a tabletop and can be vanquished by flipping him upside down.
In short, I do not recommend this toy.

text_fidelity_a:
Assassin’s Creed Syndicate Assassin's Gauntlet with Hidden Blade This is so much nicer than the cane sword. It fits on the left hand and the blade ejects with a snick kind of sound, and quite a bit of force. It's spring loaded, and if you look very closely you can see the spring, but I could imagine the "original" was the same. It's heavy leather and has gorgeous detailing. This one is worthy of Comicon or serious cos play.

The "metal" looks aged aged, a little oxidized, and not at all like plastic. It barely feels like plastic when you run your fingers over it, only a bit too warm in the cold weather. The leather looks distressed, and a bit worn, even on the inside by the knuckles. The stitching in the leather is impeccable, and with a great eye for detail. Some of the stitches are a tad longer than others, which happens with hand sewing, not typically with machine stitching. Yes, it was clearly done by machine, but the effect is to look pre-industrial which fits the game perfectly. There is even fake dirt in the spring of the grapple line.

The buckles on top are non-functional. It stays on with velcro straps on the bottom. It fits my small woman hands only barely and I imagine would be fine on a fairly tall man as well.

As with the cane, this is not for kids. The blade is on the sharp side, as is the assassin logo grapple point (I didn't notice in the game that the hook is the logo -- very cool detail). It could do some damage, especially if pointed to the eyes, and the grapple hook is a bit delicate looking. Nothing serious, but handle with some care.
text_fidelity_b: Assassin’s Creed Syndicate Assassin's Gauntlet with Hidden Blade

text_fidelity_a:
Bop It XT Finding a children's toy that can actually entertain....especially during a time (in our country) where kids spend most of there time on the IPod Touch, Xbox, WII, PSP, computers etc. is difficult. We live in a society of computer generated video games, computer enhanced movies, 3D, 4D, special effects, etc, and I find myself asking my kids -what happened to Connect 4, Twister, Simon, UNO, Clue, Life, Scrabble, PAC Man and Monopoly? Basically my childhood was filled with memories of playing these kinds of games, meaning those that essentially force you to interact with people. Under this belief, seeing the "Bop It " I thought maybe ...just maybe my kids (10 & 13) would enjoy playing this on family night. Believe it or not, while it is not animated and gloomy, it gave us hours of pure, clean fun. We battled each other. We laughed and teased. While the game kind of reminded me of Simon, it was surprisingly a bit more complicated. For Simon you just have to remember the color sequences, while the Bop challenges you to complete several tasks.....to pull, twist, flick, roll... quickly or you're out. The minute you miss, you have to start again. There is also a commentator giving the score, and teasing the player. My 13-year-old thought that this would be fun game to take on road trips (to play between all of his other electronics), while my 10-year-old is more determined than ever to beat his present score. Both found "Bop It" to be an easy to understand/fun game that promotes coordination and interacting with others. I highly recommend it.

It's light-weight and easy to carry.
It's stylish. Looks a little Jazzy...each task is a different color and shape.
It would definitely teach kids to listen. Following directions is a crucial element for playing the game.
text_fidelity_b: Bop It XT

text_fidelity_a: Brainwaves: The Astute Goose - A Kosmos Game from Thames & Kosmos | Fun, Scientist Approved, Family-Friendly Games to Sharpen Your Mind & Train Your Brain, for Ages 8+ This card game can be played solo or with up to five players. It is intended for ages eight and up. The large cards are easy to hold and the things you're supposed to memorize on each card are clear to see. There are 25 suspect cards which include variations in color, clothing, and animals. You place three to six of these cards out (depending on the difficulty level you desire) and memorize each card before turning them upside down. There are six number cards that you place above each suspect so that you know which suspect to talk about when you roll the dice. The dice roll tells you which suspect to talk about and which feature (color, clothing, or animal) that you need to remember correctly for that suspect. If the player is able to correctly remember that feature, they keep the card and score a point, but if they remember wrong, the rest of the players each have a chance to guess until someone gets it right or no one does. That suspect card is replaced with a new one, and everyone has a chance to look at the new card. Thus, you are constantly having to remember new information for each position. This can be a fun way to train your brain to remember better, but some people might find it too frustrating.
text_fidelity_b: Brainwaves: The Astute Goose - A Kosmos Game from Thames & Kosmos | Fun, Scientist Approved, Family-Friendly Games to Sharpen Your Mind & Train Your Brain, for Ages 8+

Schylling Sea Monkeys Ocean Zoo - Colors May Vary [[VIDEOID:e1253051a67b2634f9e78ac021248ab6]] I will be the first person to admit that I purchased these because I always wanted Sea Monkeys as a kid but for some reason I never got them.

The video was shot on day 5 after I put the eggs in. There are quite a few little guys swimming around it the water and they are doing fantastic. I used spring water in their tank, kept my hands and fingers OUT of the tank and placed them in a sunny window during the day and I don't move the tank around much at all. I also aerate them for about 20 seconds every other day with a small air pump and stone that is made for fishbowls, the smallest one you can find.

Mine hatched the day after I put the eggs in.

When the kit arrived, I rinsed it out with the spring water after taking everything out of it. Then I filled it to the fill line with spring water, put the lid on it and let it sit for 24 hours.

The next day, I poured the water purifier in. I didn't stir it, I didn't mess with it at all. I poured the pack in and then put the lid back on the tank.

Next day I aerated the water then poured in the eggs. Again, no stirring or anything. I left it alone, put the lid back on and walked away.

The next day, low and behold I had teeny tiny babies swimming around.

Fed them on the 5th day after they hatched, which was a few hours before I took that video footage.

I'll update again when they are larger but so far I'm really getting a kick out of this. It would appear that the secret is less is more, spring water, don't move the tank around and a lot of patience.
text_fidelity_b: Schylling Sea Monkeys Ocean Zoo - Colors May Vary

We played late into the night and still talk about some of the awesome and amazing combos! (it's hard to beat three Jason's made of lava - even if you have the hummus the card). So much laughter and I look forward to playing it anytime I can!

For those interested on how we played as a large group: we divided up into teams of two or three. Each team got one white (character) card and two black (attribute) cards. They had a minute or so to talk about strategy amongst themselves. Then - the SuperFight was on! We went around the group and each team got to tell everyone about their character (& abilities) and then debate with each other on why they would win. Everyone as a group agreed or disagreed depending on the strength of the debate. We didn't keep score, but just round by round. Lots of fun and easy to play anywhere!

Fisher-Price 3-in-1 Bounce, Stride and Ride Elephant A good toy for toddlers, the Fisher Price 3 in 1 Bounce, Ride and Stride Elephant helps youngsters develop while having fun. The toy lets then bounce, ride, and walk along as they listen to the sounds and enjoy the light up buttons and songs.

This toy is intended for toddlers under the age of 3 and most will take to it right away. Those on the younger side will like bouncing more than anything while those toward the upper end of the recommended age range will like riding and pushing. My youngest child is outside of the recommended age range, but she is lightweight for her age and liked riding the most. It takes a little bit of effort, but with just a small amount of leg power, young children can push themselves along without any assistance.

Kids will love the sounds and lights that are part of this toy. The good news for parents is that you can shut off the sounds- a feature you don’t always get with similar toys. This is nice for adults who get impatient with the constant sounds coming from kids’ toys. In truth, the sound isn’t that loud or that bad with this toy, but it’s nice to know that it can be shut off, if desired.

A toy that encourages activity, keeps kids interested, and helps them develop has all the makings of a keeper and this toy is just that. The price could turn some people away, but it’s not too bad and the fun and other advantages make this toy worth the money.

The set takes an hour or two to build, if you’re not in a hurry. As always, the printed step-by-step LEGO building instructions are very clear.
